name: Bodhi Manda Zen Center
aka: Bodhi Manda Zen Center of Rinzai-ji
technique: Zazen (sitting meditation), chanting, kinhin (walking meditation), and samu (work practice) in the traditional Rinzai Zen monastic style
teacherAccess: Resident Abbess (Jiun Hosen, Osho) and staff provide guidance; formal dokusan (teacher interviews) offered during sesshin
retreatOptions: Guest lodging with a two-night minimum stay; monthly weekend zazenkai (3-4 days) and weeklong sesshin offered several times a year, plus two-month spring and fall monastic training periods and a one-month winter program
schedule: Daily practice begins at 5 AM with zazen and chanting in the Sutra Hall; sesshin adds a rigorous meditation schedule with dokusan, silent formal meals, and daily dharma talks; the center is closed Mondays and Tuesdays
cost: Guest lodging is $100/night for one person or $175/night for a couple (two-night minimum, children 12 and under free); zazenkai (3 days) is $200-250 all-inclusive; sesshin is $450-600 (5 days) or $600-810 (7 days) all-inclusive depending on shared or private room

pricePerDay.notes: Published guest lodging rate: $100/night for one person, $175/night for a couple (two-night minimum). Sesshin (7 days, all-inclusive) works out to roughly $86-116/night separately.

workNotes: Samu (work practice) is a core part of daily monastic life, sesshin, and the seasonal monastic training periods; short-term lodging guests are not required to do samu but may join daily practice.
foodNotes: Home-cooked vegetarian meals are served buffet-style in the dining hall for $15/person/meal when available; sesshin and zazenkai fees include all meals, but lodging-only guests must confirm meal availability in advance or can dine in the village of Jemez Springs.
about: Bodhi Manda Zen Center is a Rinzai Zen Buddhist practice and retreat center in Jemez Springs, New Mexico, founded in 1973 after a student of Zen Master Joshu Sasaki Roshi found the site's natural hot springs and persuaded him to teach there. The community trains in a classic Rinzai monastic form built around zazen, chanting, kinhin, and samu, with daily sitting beginning at 5 AM in the historic Sutra Hall and Zendo, a building whose timbers have been tree-ring dated to the early 1880s, making it one of the oldest structures in Jemez Springs. Guests can stay in shared or private rooms with a required two-night minimum, and overnight visitors have access to the center's on-site natural hot springs. Beyond casual lodging, the Bodhi offers monthly weekend zazenkai, weeklong sesshin retreats, full moon sittings, and extended spring and fall monastic training periods, with all-inclusive fees covering meals, lodging, and program.
